content: The test image shows a cross-section of a corn ear with white cottony mold growing from the center/cob area, with kernels showing tan/brownish discoloration and some pinkish streaking. This points to an ear rot disease. Let me examine reference images for the top candidates.

The Trichoderma shows dark green mold (doesn't match) and Common smut shows white galls (doesn't match). The test image — a cross-section of the ear tip with white cottony mold in the center and tan/brownish discolored kernels — points strongly toward Fusarium. Let me view two more references to confirm.

**Analysis summary:**

**Test image features:**
- Cross-sectional end view of a corn ear (looking at the tip)
- **White cottony mold** concentrated in the center (cob/silk channel area)
- Kernels are yellowish/tan with **brownish discoloration** and mild **pinkish/reddish streaking**
- Some kernels appear shrunken/dimpled

**Differential reasoning:**
- **Fusarium**: White to pink/salmon cottony mold, kernels tan/brown or starburst-streaked — closely matches
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella**: Pinkish-white to **pink-red** mold at the tip via silk channel — the mold here is more white than pink-red, and Gibberella reference images showed darker/more intensely colored husks
- **Ear_rots_Diplodia**: White mold starting from the **base** — this is a tip view showing central mold, doesn't fit
- **Ear_rots_Trichoderma**: Dark green mold — ruled out
- **Ear_rots_Aspergillus**: Olive-green powdery mold — ruled out

The white cottony mold with surrounding tan/brown kernel discoloration and only mild pinkish tint is most consistent with **Fusarium** ear rot. Gibberella would be expected to show more intense red-pink mold and the reference images showed much darker coloration overall.
